description: We are Coder Knights, a student team passionate about coding, AI, web development, data, and space technology. We enjoy building practical solutions and solving real-world problems. We are looking for members interested in AI/ML, software, UI/UX, data analysis, space science, and creative ideas. No prior hackathon experience is required.
summary:
CrewPulse is a science-first health monitoring platform designed to support astronaut health and wellness during space missions. It brings important health indicators—including heart rate, blood pressure, body temperature, sleep, mood, and activity—into a unified dashboard, helping users observe changes and understand their health trends over time.

The platform is designed around the challenges of spaceflight, such as isolation, altered gravity, radiation exposure, disrupted sleep, and limited access to immediate medical support. It aims to make health information easier to understand through visual analytics, personal baselines, wellness check-ins, and evidence-informed guidance.

CrewPulse is intended as a decision-support and self-monitoring tool, not a diagnostic medical system. By combining accessible visualizations with NASA research resources, it explores how astronauts could better track their well-being and communicate meaningful health changes during long-duration missions.
details:
CrewPulse is a web-based astronaut health monitoring and mission wellness platform designed to make crew health information easier to track, understand, and communicate during space missions.

The platform organizes health indicators such as heart rate, blood pressure, body temperature, sleep duration, mood, and physical activity into a unified dashboard. Its analytics are designed to help users observe personal trends, identify changes from individual baselines, and understand when additional attention may be needed.

CrewPulse considers the five major hazards of human spaceflight: space radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, altered gravity, and hostile environments. It focuses on continuous self-monitoring, clear visualizations, wellness check-ins, and evidence-informed health guidance.

The project is built using [actual frontend technologies], [actual backend technologies], and [actual database]. Its architecture is designed to support secure health records, data visualization, and future offline operation for missions with communication delays.

NASA Human Research Program resources inform the project's understanding of spaceflight health risks. CrewPulse is a research and decision-support prototype, not a certified medical device. It does not diagnose conditions or replace professional medical judgment.

Its intended impact is to explore how accessible, science-informed software can help astronauts monitor their well-being and support more informed health discussions during long-duration missions.
